correctness.rationale: At μ=0 the mean resets to C and in (d,z) the exact map is (K sin(z)d,z+d), K=2h. Full real periodicity forces d_1=-d_0; d_0=0 gives no primitive two-cycle, and otherwise both charges satisfy sin(z)=-1/K. This proves nonexistence below K=1; at K=1 charges differ by a nonzero multiple of 2π and the step block squares to the identity. For K>1 any two distinct admissible charges give a cycle, with exchange of the two phases not producing a new orbit. The two-step block is the product of [[-1,q_j],[1,1]], with q_j=K d_j cos(z_j). Same-class gives q_1=-q_0 and eigenvalues 1±q_0, one of modulus >1. Opposite-class gives q_1=q_0 and a scalar return (1+q_0)I. Normalizing the first phase to the +θ charge by translation gives signed displacement -2θ+2πj; only j≤0 can give a sink, exactly when 0<ρ(θ+π(-j))<1. The remaining full-space multiplier is zero. Counting nonnegative integers strictly below the cutoff gives the ceiling, including omission of equality where a multiplier is -1. Both factors of the stability product are increasing in h, and at h=1 even the n=0 product is π/√3>1. Since ρ∼2√(h-1/2) and θ=arctan ρ, the claimed divergence follows. For a finite selected set of sinks the log stays away from zero on open neighborhoods of μ=0 and both orbit phases, sufficient for a local two-sided IFT even though a globally defined map for negative μ is unnecessary. D(F²-Id) is invertible, and continuity preserves strict stability, distinct phases, and inequivalence (choose disjoint neighborhoods of the distinct nonzero absolute charge displacements). Local contraction in a suitable equivalent norm gives an open basin. Take the minimum of the finite continuation radii. These are proof checks, not a re-execution of the frozen numerical diagnostic.

originality.rationale: The governing equation and claims of multistability are prior. The covered distinction is the exact primitive-two hyperbolic sink count and its divergent asymptotic for this specific map, plus the simultaneous continuation of any finite number to small positive gain. The continuation theorem itself is standard. The closest separate findings study different cycles, parameter limits or maps.
residual_risks: The Xiang et al. related DOI 10.1142/S0218127424501244 was not inspected in full; direct OA retrieval failed. The Almatroud–Pham primary source for the distinct planar model was not retrieved. These limits do not establish absence of prior equivalent work.

value.rationale: The natural multistability question becomes a complete count for a defined orbit type, with an exact boundary scaling and a theorem of arbitrarily many simultaneous open-basin sinks at small positive gain. It distinguishes strict attraction from repelling or neutral recurrence without relying on basin plots, and makes no claim about global basin sizes, all gains, or nonlinear endpoint stability.
